A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TD-VCL study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendices A–M and the checklist match across relocation; v3 adds Appendices N–O.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning experiments on MNIST/NotMNIST variants, CIFAR100-10, and TinyImageNet-10, including benchmark comparisons, per-task results, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds streaming evaluation and an early-stopping ablation in Tables 9–10.

M1.justification: The evaluated objectives and architectures remain unchanged. Appendix O.3 newly proposes retaining posteriors every m steps and combining selected TD targets, a limited optional procedural variant. Its implementation or evaluation is not reported.

E1.justification: Appendix N adds StreamingPermutedMNIST-Hard, reusing MNIST data under a distinct scenario where training chunks do not follow known task boundaries. Existing benchmark and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged. Tables 9–10 reuse the existing comparison among Online MLE, Batch MLE, VCL, VCL CoreSet, and the two TD-VCL variants; no new baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: The added streaming experiment randomly places chunk boundaries and evaluates held-out accuracy after the complete stream. Appendix O.5 adds training without early stopping. These are additional protocols; the original experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds a robustness test concerning knowledge of task boundaries and an ablation testing dependence on early stopping. The replay-buffer, single-head, per-task, and hyperparameter analyses in Appendices I–L are retained.

E5.justification: The existing ten-seed/five-seed reporting, two-standard-deviation table uncertainties, and 95% confidence intervals for plots remain unchanged. The streaming experiment also reports ten seeds, extending the existing practice without introducing a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their values. New Table 9 reports 0.89±0.02 for both TD-VCL variants versus 0.82±0.05 for VCL under streaming conditions. Table 10 reports 0.89±0.02 for TD(λ)-VCL versus 0.71±0.15 for VCL without early stopping, alongside a reported 5–10-fold training-time increase. These are additional results under different conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix N adds a formal argument for updates spanning multiple tasks, with Equations 24–27 separating update and task indices. Existing propositions and Appendix A–E derivations are unchanged. The new Equations 26–27 inconsistently repeat D_k inside products or sums indexed by j, unlike Equation 25.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: multiple-posterior variational objectives, connections to temporal-difference targets, and mitigation of catastrophic forgetting. The additional evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendices N–O substantially expand applicability and resource-limit discussion beyond v2's brief memory/tuning limitations. They address unknown task boundaries, computational and storage costs, memory-saving alternatives, λ selection, and explanations involving chunk-induced replay and overfitting. The new λ-selection rationale in O.4 runs opposite to Equation 5's weighting direction.

D1.justification: O.1 newly specifies one Monte Carlo sample for both training and inference; other additions provide storage estimates and runtime information. The code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. O.2's blanket 200-point buffer description conflicts with retained per-task limits in I/J and does not establish a change to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Bonnet et al. on Bayesian continual learning and forgetting, Zeno et al. on task-agnostic online variational Bayes, and Snoek et al. on scalable Bayesian optimization. The existing research positioning and cited works are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds Appendices N–O with a question-and-answer structure, moves the unchanged checklist before the technical appendices, and updates conference, funding, footnote, and cross-reference text. Most original prose and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the compact streaming-results Table 9 and the full-width early-stopping Table 10. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–8 retain their content and designs, with limited typesetting and page-flow changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the streaming and early-stopping experiments test two previously unexamined dependencies, while the sample-count disclosure improves reproducibility. These additions modestly strengthen the empirical documentation. The gain is limited by their narrow scope and inconsistencies in the added likelihood indices, λ advice, and buffer description; the original methods and results remain intact.
